newsitem.title: USA: Patients like HMO care, dislike service: study.
newsitem.headline: Patients like HMO care, dislike service: study.

text.p: Patients like the medical care they are getting from health maintenance organizations, although they are less satisfied with customer service and administration, a survey by CareData Reports showed.
Nationwide, eight percent of HMO members said they were not likely to re-enroll in their current health plans. One out of 10 people said they would not recommend their health plan.

The study released on Tuesday by New York-based Care Data health research firm involved data from 13 regions across the country and responses from more than 23,000 enrollees in HMOs and point of service plans.
Overall satisfaction was highest in the Boston area, with 71 percent and lowest in South Florida, where only 52 percent were content with their plans.
In New York, where CareData started tracking satisfaction in 1994, the survey found overall satisfaction rising, by nine percent with HMOs and four percent with point-of-service plans.
"Competition seems to have raised the bar in New York and health plans are jumping higher to succeed," said CareData Report president Tod Cooperman.
